candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd completes first SIMOPS biomethanol bunkering in Busan
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd has completed its first simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) bunkering of ISCC EU-certified biomethanol, marking another step in the container carrier’s transition towards alternative marine fuels. The biomethanol, supplied by Goldwind, was bunkered to the Seaspan Amazon in Busan, South Korea. According to Hapag-Lloyd, the operation was carried out while other vessel and port activities continued in parallel, allowing the bunkering process to take place without interrupting ongoing operations. The biomethanol was produced at Goldwind’s integrated facility in Hinggan League, China, before being transported through an international supply chain to South Korea. Hapag-Lloyd builds operational experience with biomethanol The operation follows the long-term green methanol supply agreement signed between Hapag-Lloyd and Goldwind in 2024. Under the agreement, Goldwind is expected to supply Hapag-Lloyd with 250,000 tonnes of a blend of bio- and e-methanol annually from the end of 2027.

candidates.title: Wan Hai completes Musang King durian shipment
candidates.excerpt: Wan Hai Lines has completed a commercial Musang King durian shipment by sea using controlled-atmosphere reefer technology. The shipment involved Malaysian tree-ripened durians, which traditionally move by air freight or in frozen form because of their short shelf life. Musang King durian shipment tests ocean transport Wan Hai used controlled-atmosphere containers to regulate oxygen and carbon dioxide levels while maintaining a stable temperature throughout the voyage. According to the carrier, the technology preserved the fruit’s freshness and quality during the nearly two-week journey. The Musang King durian shipment arrived in good condition and received positive feedback from the customer, demonstrating the potential for transporting premium fresh produce over longer distances by sea. Wan Hai said the trial could provide agricultural exporters with a more scalable and cost-effective alternative to air freight. candidates.title: Containership charter rates strengthen as mid-sized tonnage leads gains
candidates.excerpt: Containership charter rates strengthened in August, with several smaller and mid-sized vessel segments recording higher assessments compared with both July and the same period last year. According to the September 2026 edition of DynaLiners Monthly, New ConTex assessments increased month on month across all eight vessel categories covered by the index. However, the year-on-year picture remained more mixed, particularly for larger tonnage. Mid-sized tonnage records strong gains The 1,700 TEU segment recorded the strongest year-on-year increase. Its New ConTex assessment reached US$33,877 per day in August, compared with US$33,025 in July and US$26,760 in August 2025, representing an annual increase of 26.6%. The 2,500 TEU assessment rose to US$37,227 per day from US$35,423 in July. This was 6.9% higher than the US$34,840 recorded a year earlier. candidates.title: APM Terminals Aarhus and Port of Aalborg launch new rail service
candidates.excerpt: APM Terminals Aarhus and the Port of Aalborg have launched a new weekly rail service connecting the two Danish ports. The new connection gives companies in Northern Jutland direct rail access to Denmark’s largest container terminal in Aarhus. From there, cargo can connect with international shipping networks. The service also provides an alternative to the existing direct feeder connection between Aalborg and Hamburg. According to the Port of Aalborg, the partnership aims to provide companies with more transport options. In addition, it supports efforts to shift more container traffic from road to rail. Weekly rail connection between Aalborg and Aarhus Initially, the train will operate once a week between the Port of Aalborg and APM Terminals Aarhus. The two partners will monitor market demand. candidates.excerpt: New York-listed containership owner Global Ship Lease (GSL) has exercised options for another two newbuildings, taking the George Youroukos-led company’s orderbook to 17 ships. The two midsize, ultra-high-reefer, wide-beam vessels are priced at about $163m in total and are scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2029. Unlike the first 15 ships in GSL’s newbuilding programme, which have already secured long-term employment, the latest pair remain open. candidates.title: d’Amico brings last leased tanker back in-house
candidates.excerpt: Italian product tanker owner d’Amico International Shipping has exercised a $14m purchase option on the 2014-built MR tanker High Fidelity, paving the way for its entire operating fleet to return to full ownership. Operating arm d’Amico Tankers is expected to take ownership of the 50,000 dwt Hyundai Vinashin-built vessel around mid-January 2027, with the final price subject to a small adjustment depending on the actual transfer date. The ship is one of the last two vessels in d’Amico’s fleet still operating under bareboat arrangements. The company currently controls 28 product tankers on the water — 16 MRs, six handysizes and six LR1s — comprising 26 owned ships and two bareboat-chartered units. The move follows d’Amico’s decision in August to exercise a $15.3m option on sister-era MR High Discovery, which is due to return to full ownership in November. Another strong week for industrial rail freight
candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. The signing took place on the same day that Huangpu Wenchong hosted a naming ceremony for three 4,488 teu container vessels built for RCL, with one of the ships delivered to the carrier on-site.
